Build a handoff someone can act on

An escalation often arrives with a long customer thread, internal guesses, screenshots, and several attempted fixes. Nema can prepare a compact packet that preserves the evidence and the one question the next owner needs to answer.

Supply the case, approved customer context, relevant knowledge, and selected Slack discussion. Ask Nema to separate reported impact, observed facts, hypotheses, and missing information. The support lead sets severity and chooses the owner.

Preserve the incident timeline

A useful timeline records when the customer first reported the problem, which environment or account was affected, what changed, and what the team tried. Each entry should link back to the source rather than merging several statements into one confident claim.

If two records conflict, keep both visible. If a screenshot lacks a timestamp or an error cannot be reproduced, say so. Engineering can then begin with the evidence instead of repeating the whole discovery process.

Draft a structured bug handoff

Give Nema your issue template and the escalation packet. It can draft reproduction steps, observed and expected behavior, impact, environment details, attachments, and possible related issues. Similar issues should be labeled as candidates, not declared duplicates without review.

The engineer or support lead chooses severity, ownership, and whether to create the issue. A supported issue creation should show the exact title, description, labels, and project before approval, then post the created link back into the thread.

Prepare a customer reply

Nema can use the current case and approved knowledge to draft a reply. Ask it to state what the team knows, what remains under investigation, and what the customer should do next. The agent verifies the account context and edits the tone before sending.

A draft needs no artificial action approval, but the send does. Customer data should stay within an appropriate audience. Do not copy a private case into a broad product channel just because the requester can read it.

Find gaps in support knowledge

Repeated unresolved cases can expose missing or conflicting documentation. Provide a bounded set of cases and the current articles. Nema can identify repeated questions, cite examples, and draft an outline for the knowledge owner.

The owner decides whether the sample supports a new article and which guidance is correct. Nema should not turn a few cases into a claim about all customers.

Start with one real handoff shape

Choose one approved case that includes a customer thread, one image or file, and an internal discussion. Review every timeline entry and link, then edit the issue draft before approving its creation.

Questions from support teams

Is Nema customer-facing?

This workflow uses Nema inside the team. Customer replies remain drafts until an authorized agent reviews and sends them.

Can Nema read our help desk?

Confirm the exact help-desk connection in your setup. You can prepare the first handoff from an authorized case export.

How should we handle customer permissions?

Use only records the requester may access and choose a Slack audience allowed to see the result. Restricted details should stay out of broad channels.
